'''Pan Jianwei''' ({{zh|s=潘建伟|p=Pān Jiànwěi}}; born 11 March 1970) is a Chinese academic administrator and quantum physicist. He is a [[university administrator]] and professor of physics at the [[University of Science and Technology of China]]. Pan is known for his work in the field of [[quantum entanglement]], [[quantum information]] and [[quantum computer]]s. In 2017, he was named one of [[Nature's 10]], which labelled him "Father of Quantum".<ref name="Natures10">{{cite news|url=https://www.nature.com/immersive/d41586-017-07763-y/index.html|author=Elizabeth Gibney|title=Nature's 10|access-date=2019-09-15|archive-date=2017-12-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171219052227/http://www.nature.com/immersive/d41586-017-07763-y/index.html|url-status=live}}</ref> He is an academician of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] and the [[World Academy of Sciences]] and Executive Vice President of the [[University of Science and Technology of China]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ustc.edu.cn/info/1007/6940.htm|title=潘建伟-中国科学技术大学|lang=Chinese|access-date=2020-10-21|archive-date=2020-12-12|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201212153058/https://www.ustc.edu.cn/info/1007/6940.htm|url-status=live}}</ref> He also serves as one of the Vice Chairman of [[Jiusan Society]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.93.gov.cn/bsjs-ldcy-zxfzx-pjwfzx/index.html|title=潘建伟副主席_九三学社中央委员会|lang=Chinese|access-date=2020-10-20|archive-date=2020-12-04|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201204084428/http://www.93.gov.cn/bsjs-ldcy-zxfzx-pjwfzx/index.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Pan was born in [[Dongyang]], [[Jinhua]], [[Zhejiang]] province in 1970. In 1987, he entered the [[University of Science and Technology of China]] (USTC), from which he received his bachelor's and master's degrees. He received his PhD from the [[University of Vienna]] in Austria, where he studied and worked in the group led by Nobel prize winning physicist [[Anton Zeilinger]].<ref name=ykzhao/>

==Contributions==
Pan's team demonstrated five-photon entanglement in 2004.<ref>{{cite journal|vauthors=Zhao Z, Chen YA, Zhang AN, Yang T, Briegel HJ, Pan JW|date=July 2004|title=Experimental demonstration of five-photon entanglement and open-destination teleportation|journal=[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]|volume=430|issue=6995|pages=54–8|arxiv=quant-ph/0402096|bibcode=2004Natur.430...54Z|doi=10.1038/nature02643|pmid=15229594|s2cid=4336020}}</ref> Under his leadership, the world's first quantum satellite launched successfully in August 2016 as part of the [[Quantum Experiments at Space Scale]], a Chinese research project.<ref>{{cite web|author=Nomaan Merchant|url=https://phys.org/news/2016-08-china-quantum-satellite-major-space.html|title=China's launch of quantum satellite major step in space race|date=2016-08-16|access-date=2019-09-15|archive-date=2019-10-17|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191017173246/https://phys.org/news/2016-08-china-quantum-satellite-major-space.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.newscientist.com/article/2101071-china-launches-worlds-first-quantum-communications-satellite/|title=China launches world's first quantum communications satellite|author=Aron, Jacob|date=2016-08-16|access-date=2019-09-15|archive-date=2019-07-10|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190710040708/https://www.newscientist.com/article/2101071-china-launches-worlds-first-quantum-communications-satellite/|url-status=live}}</ref> In June 2017, Pan's team used their quantum satellite to demonstrate entanglement with satellite-to-ground total summed lengths between 1600km and 2400km and entanglement distribution over 1200km between receiver stations.<ref>J. Yin, Y. Cao, Y.- H. Li, S.- K. Liao, L. Zhang, J.- G. Ren, W.- Q. Cai, W.- Y. Liu, B. Li, H. Dai, G.- B. Li, Q.- M. Lu, Y.- H. Gong, Y. Xu, S.- L. Li, F.- Z. Li, Y.- Y. Yin, Z.- Q. Jiang, M. Li, J.- J. Jia, G. Ren, D. He, Y.- L. Zhou, X.- X. Zhang, N. Wang, X. Chang, Z.- C. Zhu, N.- L. Liu, Y.- Ao. Chen, C.- Y. Lu, R. Shu, C.- Z. Peng, J.- Y. Wang, and J.- W. Pan "Satellite-based entanglement distribution over 1200 kilometers", ''[[Science (journal)|Science]]'', '''356''', 6343, 1140-1144, (2017) {{doi|10.1126/science.aan3211}}</ref>

In 2021, ''[[Physics World]]'' reported that Pan had led two teams which built two quantum computers, one of which used superconducting circuits and the other of which used photons.<ref name="PhysWorld2021">{{cite news |title=Quantum advantage takes a giant leap in optical and superconducting systems |url=https://physicsworld.com/a/quantum-advantage-takes-a-giant-leap-in-optical-and-superconducting-systems/ |work=Physics World |date=October 26, 2021 |quote=Two different quantum computers, one using light ([[Jiuzhang (quantum computer)|Jiuzhang]]) and the other superconducting circuits...were used to calculate the output probabilities of quantum circuits.}}</ref> The device using superconducting circuits, named "''Zuchongzhi 2.1''", was claimed to be one million times faster than its nearest competitor, Google's ''Sycamore''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/life-style/gadgets-and-tech/china-scientists-programmable-quantum-computers-b1946018.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220524/https://www.independent.co.uk/life-style/gadgets-and-tech/china-scientists-programmable-quantum-computers-b1946018.html |archive-date=2022-05-24 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live|title = China builds world's fastest programmable quantum computers|website = [[Independent.co.uk]]|date = 31 October 2021}}</ref>

==Awards and recognition==
Pan was elected to the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] in 2011 at the age of 41, making him one of the youngest [[Chinese Academy of Sciences|CAS]] academicians.<ref>{{cite web|title=41岁潘建伟教授当选最年轻中国科学院院士|url=https://sias.ustc.edu.cn/2016/0408/c3121a26758/page.htm|publisher=sias.ustc.edu.cn|access-date=2 May 2022|archive-date=14 December 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231214220938/https://sias.ustc.edu.cn/2016/0408/c3121a26758/page.htm|url-status=live}}</ref> He was then elected to the World Academy of Sciences in 2012 and won the International Quantum Communication Award in the same year.<ref>{{cite web|author=Mason Coultrane|title=Quantum Communication Takes Another Leap Between Beijing and Shanghai|url=http://en.yibada.com/articles/12269/20150206/quantum-communication-takes-another-leap-between-beijing-and-shanghai.htm|website=Yibada|date=2015-02-06|access-date=2019-09-15|archive-date=2019-04-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190425074749/http://en.yibada.com/articles/12269/20150206/quantum-communication-takes-another-leap-between-beijing-and-shanghai.htm|url-status=live}}</ref>

In April 2014, he was appointed Vice President of the University of Science and Technology of China.

His team's work on double quantum-teleportation was selected as the ''Physics World'' "Top Breakthrough of the Year" in 2015.<ref name="phys-world"/> His team, whose members include Peng Chengzhi, [[Chen Yu'ao]], [[Lu Chao-Yang]], and Chen Zengbing, won the [[State Natural Science Award]] (First Class) in 2015.<ref name="2015-state"/>

In 2017, the journal ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]'' named Pan, along with such figures as [[Ann Olivarius]] and [[Scott Pruitt]], one of the top 10 people who made "a significant impact in science either for good or for bad", with the label "Father of Quantum" given to Pan.<ref name="Natures10"/> The same year he won the [[Future Science Prize]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Nature Research Custom Media |date=2017 |title=Future Science Prize 2017 |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/d42473-022-00326-4 |journal=Nature Portafolio |language=en}}</ref>

Pan was included in [[Time (magazine)|''Time'']] magazine's ''100 Most Influential People of 2018.''<ref>{{Cite magazine|title=Jian-Wei Pan: The World's 100 Most Influential People|url=https://time.com/collection/most-influential-people-2018/5238153/jian-wei-pan/|access-date=2020-09-22|magazine=Time|language=en-us|archive-date=2020-10-03|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201003044052/https://time.com/collection/most-influential-people-2018/5238153/jian-wei-pan/|url-status=live}}</ref> The same year, he became a laureate of the [[Asian Scientist 100]] by the ''[[Asian Scientist]]''.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.asianscientist.com/as100/ |title=The Asian Scientist 100 |author= <!--Not stated--> |date= |website= |publisher= [[Asian Scientist]] |access-date= 13 March 2025 |quote= |language= }}</ref>

In 2019, Pan was appointed as lead editor of ''[[Physical Review Research]]''.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.aps.org/publications/apsnews/updates/prr-pan.cfm|title=Jian-Wei Pan Appointed Lead Editor of Physical Review Research|publisher=American Physical Society|date=2019-06-11|access-date=2019-09-15|archive-date=2019-09-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190901220952/https://www.aps.org/publications/apsnews/updates/prr-pan.cfm|url-status=live}}</ref> He also received [[Optica (society)|The Optical Society]]'s [[R. W. Wood Prize]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Optical Society Names Jian-Wei Pan the 2019 R.W. Wood Prize Recipient {{!}} Optica |url=https://www.optica.org/about/newsroom/news_releases/2019/the_optical_society_names_jian-wei_pan_the_2019_r_w_wood_prize_recipient/ |access-date=2024-09-16 |website=www.optica.org}}</ref>

In 2020, Pan received the ZEISS Research Award.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.zeiss.com/corporate/int/newsroom/press-releases/zeiss-pressemitteilung/jian-wei-pan-to-receive-zeiss-research-award.html|title=Jian-Wei Pan to Receive ZEISS Research Award|date=2020-04-20|access-date=2020-10-20|archive-date=2020-10-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201021042725/https://www.zeiss.com/corporate/int/newsroom/press-releases/zeiss-pressemitteilung/jian-wei-pan-to-receive-zeiss-research-award.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

In 2026, the [[IEEE Photonics Society]] awarded Pan (together with [[Lu Chao-Yang]]) their [[IEEE_Photonics_Society#Awards|Quantum Electronics Award]] of  "For pioneering work on single photon sources and optical quantum computing"<ref>{{cite web |title=IEEE Photonics Society Quantum Electronics Award |url=https://ieeephotonics.org/awards/quantum-electronics-award/ |publisher=IEEE Photonics Society |access-date=July 25, 2026 |quote=Recognizes outstanding technical contributions to quantum electronics, either in fundamentals, applications, or in both.}}</ref>

At an award ceremony in Paris in July 2026, Pan received from [[UNESCO]] the UNESCO-Russia Mendeleev International Prize in the Basic Sciences, with the following citation: "Professor Jian-Wei Pan is a world-leading expert in quantum optics, quantum communications and quantum computation at the University of Science and Technology of China. He is recognized for his seminal contributions to large-scale secure quantum communications and scalable quantum computation. His team developed the Micius satellite, enabling quantum key distribution and quantum teleportation over thousands of kilometres, and has demonstrated quantum computational advantage, bringing the prospect of a global quantum network from theory to reality."<ref>{{cite web |title=Award Ceremony of the Third Edition of the UNESCO-Russia Mendeleev International Prize in the Basic Sciences |url=https://www.unesco.org/en/articles/award-ceremony-third-edition-unesco-russia-mendeleev-international-prize-basic-sciences-0 |access-date=July 25, 2026}}</ref>
